key_insight: PI-GMDH adaptively builds the functional form of a physics-informed solution during training, instead of fixing the representation upfront.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical way to trade accuracy, model size, and compute cost when solving coupled PDEs such as incompressible Navier–Stokes flows.
method: Progressively adds candidate functional directions using first-variation screening of the full physics + data objective.
Optimizes coefficients with block-coordinate damped Gauss-Newton updates.
Uses tensor-product Chebyshev functions to model u, v, and p on a 2D time-dependent Taylor-Green benchmark.
evidence_signal: On the reported benchmark, adaptive PI-GMDH achieved validation and held-out test losses of 5.299e-19 and 5.296e-19, with 204, 201, and 175 active functions for u, v, and p.
watch_item: The results are on a controlled synthetic benchmark, so the apparent advantage may not transfer directly to more complex real-world flows or different PDE settings.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Method of Group Data Handling: Adaptive Construction of Functional Representations with an Application to the Navier-Stokes Equations
